verdict.rationale: pnpm documents lockfile-enforced installs: in CI it automatically switches to frozen-lockfile mode and fails if the lockfile needs an update. It also guards tarball integrity, offering --update-checksums only as a narrow opt-in. The docs do not explicitly state that the lockfile yields identical resolved versions on every developer machine outside CI, so coverage is partial. A community preference for yarn3's reproducibility is general opinion, not a concrete counter-example. missing for 10: explicit documentation of frozen/lockfile-only installs on local developer machines, an explicit cross-machine identical-resolution guarantee, independent hands-on corroboration of reproducibility.

support.subject: As a developer, I can install dependencies from a lockfile and get the exact same resolved versions on every machine

citations.quote: When pnpm detects that it is running in CI, it switches to frozen-lockfile mode automatically.
In a CI environment, installation fails if a lockfile is present but needs an update.
--update-checksums is the narrowly-scoped opt-in for the legitimate case (e.g. a registry rewrote its tarballs and you've verified the new bytes are correct).
The lockfile is left untouched, so frozen installs still validate
